output:
To: lindqvist-family-blog
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Big news: Fernhollow Photo is officially a real business!!

Okay. Deep breath. I've been typing and deleting this post for about a week, so I'm just going to say it.

I'm going out on my own. Fernhollow Photo is a real, legal, actual business, and I am a person who owns one!!

Here's how it came together. Marisol closed Rosebud Lane at the end of October. She told me on October 6, and I've been shooting for her for four years, so you can imagine the phone call. Marisol basically taught me everything I know. How to read a room, how to stay calm when the timeline falls apart, how to get a stiff groom to relax by asking about his dog. If my work is any good, a big chunk of that is her. Thank you, Marisol. I owe you about a hundred coffees.

Here's the part I'm proudest of: I've been thinking about this for two years. Not in a "someday I'll quit my job and move to a cabin" way, but in a "quietly doing math in my head at every wedding" way. When the studio closed, I wasn't starting from nothing. I was just starting earlier than I'd planned.

So, the real stuff, for anyone who wants to know I'm not winging it:

I filed the LLC on October 22, on my lunch break, in my car in the parking lot outside a Fred Meyer. Fernhollow Photo LLC. I filled out the last page, hit submit, and cried a little. Just a little. There was a guy loading groceries next to me and he very politely pretended not to see. The website went live on November 1.

I already have 14 weddings booked for 2027. Six of those are couples Marisol sent my way (she told them all I was the one, which I'm still not over), and eight of them found me completely on their own. June is my busiest month, with four weddings, and the farthest one out is a September wedding at Wallowa Lake, which I am going to treat as a vacation with a camera.

My very first booking that was 100% mine was Dahlia and Ken, at Timberline on June 12. They found me through the Multnomah Falls couple photos I'd shot. No referral, no middleman, just somebody looking at my pictures and deciding they wanted me there on their day. I read Dahlia's email about four times. Then I read it to Sam. Then I read it to Pickle, who was unmoved.

For the bigger weddings, my friend Jae is going to second shoot with me, paid per wedding. Jae is great, and having a second set of eyes (and a second set of knees) is going to make a huge difference.

Dad, this one's for you, and I'm putting it in bold in my heart: health insurance is sorted. I picked a marketplace plan, and it starts January 1. I know you've been looking out for me on this, and I love you for it. I wanted you to hear it here, in writing, with no turkey involved.

I'm not going to pretend it isn't scary, because it is. It's a little terrifying to look at a calendar and know that every single one of those dates is on me now. But it's the good kind of scary, the kind where I keep catching myself grinning at nothing. I have a plan, I have people in my corner, and I have a very full calendar already. I've never been more sure about anything.

Now, the name. A few of you have asked where Fernhollow came from, so here's the story. Behind Grandma's old place in Gresham there was a trail we always called the fern hollow trail, this dip in the woods where the ferns got taller than me. It's where I took my first real pictures, on Grandma's Pentax, when I was way too young to be trusted with it. I'm sure most of them were blurry. I remember exactly how it felt, though, standing in all that green and realizing I could keep a moment if I got the light right.

Grandma, the name is for you. I wanted you to know that. You gave me the camera, and I'm pretty sure you gave me the whole idea. I'll bring a print of the business logo so you can put it on the fridge next to the Christmas group photo.

One more thing. Sam surprised me with a cake to celebrate, and it said FERNHOLLOW across the top. Except the baker, or possibly Sam, spelled it FERNHOLOW. Just one L. We looked at it for a full minute, laughed until we were wheezing, and then ate it anyway. It was delicious. If the business ever has a mascot, it's that cake.

Finally, a small request, and an actual offer. Thanksgiving at Ruthie's is on the 26th, and I'd love to bring my camera. If anybody wants some free family photos, let me know! Individual portraits, couples, the whole crew, whatever you want. Honestly, it'd be a gift to me too, because I'd love to practice on people who already love me and won't mind if I make them stand in weird light for a minute. Comment below or tell me at dinner and I'll find us a good spot before the sun goes down. (Greg, I promise you won't be freezing this time.)

Thank you all for always being the people who cheer the loudest. I can't wait to show you what comes next. I'm just getting started, and I'd love for you to be excited with me.

Love you all, see you at Ruthie's.

Tessa

P.S. Mom, yes, I'm bringing Sam, and yes, I'm bringing the rolls and the cranberry thing.
